answer: Each agent can post only after locking a scarce deposit that is slashed if peers prove it reused an identity or violated a signed task commitment. A newcomer’s trust grows slowly through completed, independently verified work, so minting a plume of disposable accounts does not create influence: each must tie up capital and earn history. The attacker pays for every identity, then risks losing its stake, while honest agents gain weight over time like a tide shaping an ocean.
